clue.text: Our lowest denomination forsaken as Epiphany came

parts.note: the penny is the smallest British coin, our lowest denomination
forsaken means dropped or abandoned

explanation.surface: Someone muses that the humble penny has been abandoned just as a revelation arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' is a link word. The phrase splits into the smallest coin and a word for abandoned.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a sudden moment of understanding, which is what an epiphany is.

clue.text: As exemplified by "Three, two, one, dive!"?

definitions.text: As exemplified by "Three, two, one, dive!"?

parts.words: As exemplified by "Three, two, one, dive!"?
parts.note: a countdown runs from high numbers to low, and a dive goes downward, so the example shows the arrangement twice over

explanation.surface: A diver counts down before plunging off the board.
explanation.definitionFit: A countdown lists numbers from largest to smallest, the arrangement this phrase names, and the dive adds a literal downward motion.

clue.text: Heed voting in new assembly and signal assent

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are put together afresh in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Delegates are told to pay attention to the vote in a newly formed assembly and to show agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in new assembly' rearranges the ten letters of HEED VOTING; 'and' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone a nod is an idiom for approving or authorising, a sign of agreement.

clue.text: Seriousness of something that affects all on earth

definitions.meaning: solemnity or weightiness of manner or situation

definitions.text: something that affects all on earth
definitions.meaning: the force pulling every object on the planet towards its centre

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both solemn weightiness and the physical force of attraction acting on every body on the planet.

clue.text: Bear precisely half of ridicule

indicators.note: exactly the first half of the synonym is kept, the reduplicated word cut in two

parts.note: to ridicule or dismiss an idea is to ...-... it

explanation.surface: Someone has a bear exactly half-mocked.
explanation.walkthrough: The verb for dismissing scornfully is a doubled word; half of it is the name of A. A. Milne's bear.
explanation.definitionFit: Winnie-the-Pooh is the famous fictional bear of A. A. Milne's stories.

clue.text: Pass a diamond to Nick in play and finish in lowest position

parts.note: to pass something to someone is to reach it to them
rock is slang for a diamond
Nick Bottom is the weaver in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream

explanation.surface: In a game, someone hands a gem to a player called Nick, then ends up last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link word. Nick is not a verb meaning steal here but the first name of Bottom in Shakespeare's comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to sink to the lowest possible point, so ending up at the bottom.

clue.text: Topple inside foxhole and return to reality

parts.note: to topple is to fall, to come down
a hunted fox that goes to earth has hidden in its burrow

explanation.surface: A soldier falls into a foxhole and snaps back to reality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is a link word. A fox's burrow is called its earth, so 'gone to earth' means taken refuge underground.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to stop daydreaming and face the practical facts again.

clue.text: After church, stranger's in better spirits

indicators.note: the second piece is placed after the first, as the clue's opening word says

parts.note: stranger means eerier, weirder

explanation.surface: After a church service, a newcomer is in a happier mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stranger' reads as a person but is the comparative adjective; the 's is 'is' and gives no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheerier is a comparative meaning happier, in a brighter mood.

clue.text: Gold, for example, possible in location north of California

parts.note: OR is the heraldic term for gold
EG is the abbreviation for exempli gratia, for example
on means feasible, as in 'that's not on'

explanation.surface: Gold, for instance, might be found in a place north of California.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gold, for example' looks like one phrase meaning ore, a tempting false path that leaves a letter over; gold is the heraldic tincture and 'for example' its own abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Oregon is the US state on the Pacific coast directly bordering California to the north.

clue.text: Indian old man gripped by pain

indicators.note: the word for father is held inside the word for pain

parts.note: an ache is a pain
old man is slang for father, PA

explanation.surface: An elderly man of Native American heritage is in pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indian' here means a Native American people.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apache are a group of Native American peoples, once called Indians.

clue.text: Water and oil, say, for cars and buses, say

definitions.meaning: liquids that carry pigment in painting are called media or carriers

explanation.definitionFit: In painting, the liquid in which pigment is suspended is its vehicle; cars and buses are road vehicles.

clue.text: Here answer's having no name

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for answer
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for name; that the letters of 'no name' read backwards contain the answer is a coincidence, not the setter's device

explanation.surface: An answer here is said to be anonymous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having' is a link word. 'Anon!' is the old reply of a summoned servant, meaning 'Coming!', so it stands for 'Here!'; 'having no name' tempts as the definition but wordplay must fill it.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespearean usage a servant called for answers 'Anon!', meaning coming at once, the same response as 'Here!'.

clue.text: Go ballistic and attack Thatcher's work, perhaps?

parts.note: to hit is to attack
a thatcher builds a straw covering on top of a house

explanation.surface: Someone flies into a rage and goes after Margaret Thatcher's record in office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is a link word. The capital T makes us think of the former Prime Minister; a thatcher is a craftsman who roofs with straw.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to lose one's temper explosively, just as going ballistic does.

clue.text: Garments in sorry state abandoned in Irish trash

indicators.note: abandoned means wild or unrestrained, so the letters run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: Clothes in a pitiful condition have been dumped among Irish rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' rearranges IRISH TRASH; 'in' is a link word. The definition points to clothes worn by penitents, people who are sorry.
explanation.definitionFit: Coarse shirts of goat hair were worn next to the skin by penitents, who are by definition sorry for their sins.

clue.text: Hospital eyeing changes in healthy practice

indicators.note: the letters of the word are altered in order

explanation.surface: A hospital is watching how things change in its health routines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eyeing' reads as watching but is anagram fodder; 'in' is a link word between wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Hygiene is the practice of cleanliness that keeps people healthy.

clue.text: Fruit from tree criminal put in sack

indicators.note: the word for a criminal is placed inside the word for sack

parts.note: to sack someone is to fire them
a con is a convict, a criminal

explanation.surface: Fruit taken from a tree is stuffed into a sack by a criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sack' looks like a bag but is the verb meaning dismiss.
explanation.definitionFit: A conifer's cone holds its seeds, its fruit in the loose sense.

clue.text: River fish moving under 4

parts.note: the Fal is a river in Cornwall
the ling is a fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A fish in a river swims beneath something.
explanation.walkthrough: 4 is GRAVITY, so the definition is moving under gravity. The Fal is a river in Cornwall, in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dropping is moving down under the pull of gravity, the answer at 4.

clue.text: Somewhat outraged, I answer for some players

indicators.note: Somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone, a little indignant, responds on behalf of a group of actors.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft definition included 'for', which cannot replace the answer in a sentence; 'for' is a link word and the definition is 'some players'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tragedians are actors who specialise in tragic roles, so they are some of the players on a stage.

clue.text: Job, for example, that's bound to be completed

definitions.meaning: Job is one of the ... of the Old Testament
a printed volume is finished when its pages are bound

explanation.definitionFit: Job is a volume of the Bible, and a printed volume is finished by binding its pages.

clue.text: Embraced by a friend, supporting with very positive response

indicators.note: the inner pieces are held within the outer ones

parts.note: a pal is a friend
pro means in favour of, supporting

explanation.surface: A friend gives a hug and a warm welcome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link word; PROV goes between the A and P of APAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Approval is a favourable reaction, saying yes to something.

clue.text: As this, best is not very different from worst

definitions.text: As this, best is not very different from worst

parts.words: As this, best is not very different from worst
parts.note: used as a doing word, to best someone and to worst them both mean to defeat them

explanation.surface: Someone observes that the best and the worst are much alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as a part of speech for actions, best and worst both mean defeat, though as adjectives they are opposites.

clue.text: Aboard carrier, there's work to be done

parts.note: aboard means in, as on a vehicle
a tray is something that carries things

explanation.surface: On an aircraft carrier, there is still work to do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrier' suggests a ship but is a tray that carries cups or papers.
explanation.definitionFit: An office in-tray is the receptacle holding papers still to be dealt with.

clue.text: Visitor to our world from remote parts

indicators.note: parts as a verb means divides and redistributes, so the letters are split up and rearranged

explanation.surface: An alien visitor arrives from distant regions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parts' looks like a noun for regions but signals the letters of REMOTE rearranged; 'from' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A shooting star is a body from space that enters Earth's atmosphere, a visitor to our planet.

clue.text: Total assets of the town diverted to protect monarch

indicators.note: the letter for the monarch is guarded inside the rearranged letters
diverted means turned aside, so the letters take a different course

parts.note: R stands for rex or regina, king or queen

explanation.surface: A town's entire wealth is redirected to safeguard the king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diverted' rearranges THE TOWN to NETWOTH, and 'to protect' puts R inside it; 'of' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Net worth is what someone owns minus what they owe, their whole financial value.
